afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 271112
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
412 AM MST Thu Aug 27 2026

.UPDATE...12Z Aviation Discussion

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Extreme Heat Warnings remain in effect through Saturday with
  areas of Major to Extreme Heat Risk, despite temperatures 
  slowly decreasing.

- Today and Friday will bring low end chances for showers and a
  few thunderstorms, focused more across southern and central
  Arizona.

- A low pressure system nearing the region over the weekend will
  bring much better chances for rain, including a chance of strong
  to severe storms across southern Arizona from mainly on Sunday
  or Monday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
An unseasonably strong subtropical ridge remains positioned
directly over the Desert Southwest, but it is getting infiltrated
by a good amount of high level moisture peeled away from the 
remnants of TC Iselle. Water vapor imagery shows a decent stream
of upper level moisture just west and southwest of northern Baja
into Arizona. We anticipate partly to mostly cloudy skies across
southeast California and partly cloudy skies over Arizona today
providing a slight reprieve from the scorching temperatures.
Despite the higher clouds, highs are still expected to easily top
110 degrees across the lower deserts today, but they should be a
few degrees cooler than yesterday's.

In the lower levels, a modest Gulf surge of moisture is currently
working its way into the area with 65-70 degree dew points already 
into Yuma and the Imperial Valley and eventually to around 60
degrees in the Phoenix area later this morning. However, even with
some improvement in moisture for today forecast soundings show
little support for convection. Low level mixing ratios will at
most reach 8 g/kg this afternoon which is barely adequate for even
high terrain storms for an ideal monsoon season day. The 
continued strong subsidence from the ridge overhead should be 
enough to keep any potential convection confined to higher terrain
areas this afternoon/early evening with at most isolated 
coverage. Slightly more favorable conditions should at least allow
for some more scattered convection over far southeast Arizona 
which eventually may be enough to kick off a northward progressing
outflow toward Pinal and Maricopa Counties late in the evening. 
The HRRR suggests a combination of this potential outflow with 
some mid-level moisture advection and/or gravity waves from more 
organized convection over Sonora may be enough to spark off some 
elevated late evening showers and weak storms. Have adjusted PoPs
upward to 10-20% over south-central Arizona from 10 PM to 3 AM 
tonight to account for this potential.

Friday is shaping up to be relatively quiet through the majority
of the day with no additional moisture advection tonight and
through the first half of Friday. The higher level moisture and
clouds for today are also expected to push out of the area 
leaving more sunshine for Friday. CAMs show less convective 
activity than today, but that is only through Friday afternoon. 
The subtropical high is also forecast to weaken and push into 
northern New Mexico. Given the lowering heights, but more 
sunshine forecast highs on Friday are very similar to today's, 
keeping widespread Major to Extreme HeatRisk over the area. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
A significant pattern change is set to begin this weekend with a
large Pacific trough slowly moving southeastward across the
Western U.S., eventually pushing the subtropical high into the
Southern Plains by Sunday. Our main forecast concern with this
change will be the increasingly favorable conditions for
thunderstorms, especially by Sunday and Monday. The influence of
the trough may occur as early as late Friday night and early
Saturday as a relatively strong jet streak moves through
California into the Great Basin. This should result in increasing
upper level support for showers and thunderstorms, but we will
also have to have enough moisture. For now, guidance is unclear on
the rain chances for early Saturday, but the NBM is trying to put
a 30-40% chance in after midnight. The daytime hours Saturday are
just as unclear as moisture is likely to continue to improve, but
will it be enough to overcome a modest capping inversion. 
Guidance does show PoPs of 30-40% during the evening hours 
Saturday from Phoenix and areas to the north and east of Phoenix,
but little chance to the west. Temperatures Saturday will cool a 
bit from Friday, but there should still be enough residual heat to
push daytime highs to around 110 degrees across the western lower
deserts to 107-109 degrees in the Phoenix area.

Sunday into possibly Monday very well could be quite active as
guidance is pointing at very good moisture advection into Arizona,
somewhat directed by a passing tropical system to the southwest of
southern Baja. Atmospheric parameters improve on Sunday with
MUCAPEs anywhere from 1000-2000 J/kg and little if any CIN during
the afternoon hours. The presence of the trough over or just to
the northwest of our area should also provide some modest shear
and upper level support for storm potential on Sunday and/or
Monday. Depending on the evolution of the trough, heating, and 
how much moisture gets pulled into our area, we may need to worry
about a strong to severe storm potential as well as a heavy
rainfall threat as PWATs may reach near 1.75". Drier air will also
be trying to work into western portions of our area by Sunday,
leaving little chance for rain over southeast California and
potentially southwest Arizona. NBM PoPs reflect this with at most
10-20% chances over the western deserts, but PoPs rise to 40-60%
from Phoenix and areas to the north and east of Phoenix on Sunday.
There is much higher model uncertainty going into the mid to
latter half of next week as GEFS favors moisture staying mostly in
place while the EPS favors some more significant drying. Part of
this uncertainty is due to a highly active tropic region to our
southwest which very well could influence our region at times.

Temperatures are at least slated to drop a good amount over the
weekend into early next week with forecast highs falling back to
near normal on Sunday and then at or just below the normal range
early next week. We can't even rule out having highs in the 90s
for a day across south-central Arizona if the rain activity is
widespread enough on Sunday and/or Monday. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1112Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:

No major aviation concerns will exist through the TAF period. 
Winds are expected to mostly follow light and diurnal trends
through the period. Some VCSH cannot be ruled out during the mid 
to late morning timeframe, but forecast uncertainty remains too 
high to warrant inclusion of any rainfall mention in the TAFs. If 
any SHRA were to occur, operational impacts should be minimal. 
Otherwise, a southerly outflow with gusts between 20-25kts is 
likely late tonight to near midnight before switch back easterly 
for the remainder of the the overnight period tomorrow. SCT-BKN
high clouds will persist through the period. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

No major aviation concerns are expected through the TAF period. 
Winds will follow familiar diurnal trends, and some VCSH cannot 
be ruled out during the mid to late morning timeframe, mainly for 
KBLH, but forecast uncertainty remains too high to warrant 
inclusion of any rainfall mention on the TAF. KBLH is likely to
see gusty conditions again near midnight tonight from the south 
with speeds between 20-25kts. SCT-BKN high clouds will persist
through the period. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Hot and relatively dry conditions will continue over the next
couple of days with only widely isolated showers and thunderstorms
possible. Afternoon minimum humidities will improve slightly to
15-20% through Friday before improving further over the weekend as
rain chances increase over Arizona. Winds through Friday will 
overall be light and follow diurnal tendencies, with modest 
afternoon upslope/upvalley breeziness.

&&

.CLIMATE...

Aug 29   116 in 2023    117 in 1954    117 in 2005

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

     560.

     Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Friday for AZZ556-561-562.

     569-570.

     Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT Friday for CAZ561-563-564-
     568.

&&
